title: Leptospirosis (adult, India)
subject: infectious-disease
summary: Suspect in fever with myalgia, calf tenderness or conjunctival suffusion after flood-water, field or animal exposure. Treat empirically: doxycycline for mild disease; IV penicillin or ceftriaxone for severe disease. Refer early for AKI, jaundice, bleeding or breathlessness, as pulmonary haemorrhage kills within hours.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Suspected case (NCDC): fever, headache, myalgia and prostration after exposure to animal urine or contaminated water or soil (floods, paddy fields, sewers, cattle), plus any of: calf tenderness, conjunctival suffusion, oliguria or proteinuria, jaundice, bleeding, meningism, GI upset.
Severe calf and lumbar muscle tenderness and bilateral conjunctival suffusion are characteristic; the illness may be biphasic.
Weil disease: jaundice with acute kidney injury, often with bleeding and hypotension. Jaundice typically starts after 4 to 7 days of illness.
Pulmonary haemorrhage: cough, haemoptysis (may be absent), rapidly rising breathlessness and spreading bilateral infiltrates; the commonest cause of death, often within hours to 2 days.

Clues against viral hepatitis: transaminases only modestly raised (hundreds), high bilirubin, raised CPK, neutrophilic leucocytosis, thrombocytopenia and an active urine sediment. AKI is often non-oliguric with hypokalaemia.

sections.title: Investigations
items: CBC, creatinine, urea, sodium and potassium, bilirubin and liver enzymes, CPK, urinalysis, coagulation, blood gas, chest X-ray and ECG.
Presumptive diagnosis: positive IgM ELISA or rapid test, or a single MAT titre of 100, 200 or 400 or more depending on local endemicity. Serology is often negative in the first week.
Confirmation: culture, PCR (blood in the first week), seroconversion or a fourfold rise in MAT titre on paired sera.
Test for malaria, dengue and scrub typhus at the same time; co-infections occur and management overlaps.

sections.title: Mild disease (outpatient)
items: Start antibiotics on clinical suspicion without waiting for test results; early treatment shortens and softens the illness.
Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 7 days.
Alternatives (and in pregnancy or lactation): ampicillin 500 mg orally 6-hourly or amoxicillin 500 mg orally 6-hourly for 7 days; or azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 3 days (CDC).
Review at 48 to 72 hours or earlier if urine output falls, jaundice appears, or breathlessness or bleeding develop.

sections.title: Severe disease (hospital)
items: Crystalline penicillin G 20 lakh units (2 million units) IV 6-hourly for 7 days (NCDC; CDC uses 1.5 million units 6-hourly).
OR ceftriaxone 1 g IV once daily for 7 days (CDC). NCDC 2015 lists more frequent dosing; the once-daily regimen is the internationally used, trial-supported dose.
OR cefotaxime 1 g IV 6-hourly for 7 days (NCDC).
If scrub typhus has not been excluded in severe undifferentiated fever, add doxycycline (or azithromycin) to the beta-lactam.
Watch for a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction (fever, rigors, hypotension) in the first hours after the first antibiotic dose; treat supportively and continue antibiotics.

sections.title: Refer or escalate immediately (NCDC criteria)
items: Hypotension, irregular pulse, altered consciousness or bleeding tendency.
Urine output below 400 mL/day, urea above 60 mg/dL, creatinine above 2.5 mg/dL, or uraemic features.
Bilirubin above 3 mg/dL.
Breathlessness, haemoptysis, raised respiratory rate or new chest X-ray opacities; move to ICU before respiratory failure is established.

sections.title: Organ support
items: Pulmonary haemorrhage or ARDS: early ICU, early intubation, lung-protective ventilation (tidal volume 6 mL/kg predicted body weight, plateau pressure below 30 cmH2O) with PEEP; avoid fluid overload.
AKI: start renal replacement early for oliguria, fluid overload, acidosis or uraemia; correct hypokalaemia in non-oliguric AKI. Renal recovery is usual by about 4 weeks.
Shock: cautious crystalloid boluses with reassessment, then noradrenaline to a MAP of 65 mmHg.
Bleeding is not tightly related to the platelet count; transfuse for active bleeding rather than to a number.

sections.title: Pregnancy and children
items: Pregnancy: ampicillin 500 mg 6-hourly for mild disease; IV penicillin or ceftriaxone for severe disease. Doxycycline is avoided. Leptospirosis carries a high risk of fetal loss.
Children under 8 years, mild disease: amoxicillin or ampicillin 30 to 50 mg/kg/day orally in divided doses for 7 days (NCDC).
Children, severe disease: crystalline penicillin 2 to 4 lakh units/kg/day IV in divided doses, or ceftriaxone 50 to 75 mg/kg/day IV, for 7 days (NCDC).

sections.title: Prevention
items: Rubber boots and gloves for field, sewer and flood work; avoid wading or bathing in contaminated water; cover cuts and abrasions with antiseptic before and after exposure.
Rodent control, clean surroundings and safe storage of food grains; community awareness before the monsoon.

Chemoprophylaxis (NCDC): doxycycline 200 mg once weekly during peak transmission season for high-risk workers (paddy field or canal workers) in endemic areas with case clusters; give for 6 weeks and never beyond 8 weeks.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Labelling fever with jaundice as viral hepatitis without checking creatinine, CPK and urine.
Delaying antibiotics for MAT or ELISA results.
Underestimating mild haemoptysis or tachypnoea, which can precede fatal pulmonary haemorrhage.
Treating only for leptospirosis when scrub typhus, malaria or dengue co-infection is present.

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.dose: 100 mg orally twice daily for 7 days
drugs.notes: Mild disease. Avoid in pregnancy, lactation and children under 8 years.

drugs.name: Ampicillin or amoxicillin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally 6-hourly for 7 days (children 30 to 50 mg/kg/day in divided doses)
drugs.notes: Pregnancy, lactation and children under 8 years.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally once daily for 3 days

drugs.name: Crystalline penicillin G (benzylpenicillin)
drugs.dose: 20 lakh units (2 million units) IV 6-hourly for 7 days
drugs.notes: Severe disease (NCDC). Children 2 to 4 lakh units/kg/day. CDC dose 1.5 million units 6-hourly.

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.dose: 1 g IV once daily for 7 days

drugs.name: Doxycycline chemoprophylaxis
drugs.notes: High-risk occupational exposure in peak season; 6 weeks, never beyond 8 weeks.
